question.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:\{\begin{aligned}x=2+t \\ y=-1+3t \\ z=3-2t\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,Π:2x+y-5z=63.
$$
question.worked_solution:
We can substitute the parametric expressions for $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ of the line into the equation of the plane immediately:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+y-5z & =63 \\ 2(2+t)+(-1+3t)-5(3-2t) & =63 \\ 4+2t-1+3t-15+10t & =63 \\ 15t & =75 \\ t & =5\end{aligned}
$$

To get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$, we substitute $t=5$ into the parametric equations of the line:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=2+5=7 \\ y=-1+3(5)=14 \\ z=3-2(5)=-7\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is $P(7,14,-7).$
